device.name: AgiBot X1 DH stand training environment (X1DHStandEnv)

facts.text: X1DHStandEnv.step adds the reference action when cfg.env.use_ref_actions is set, then calls LeggedRobot.step
LeggedRobot.step clips actions to +-cfg.normalization.clip_actions, simulates cfg.control.decimation physics substeps and returns (obs_buf, privileged_obs_buf, rew_buf, reset_buf, extras)
LeggedRobot.reset takes no arguments, resets every environment, steps zero actions and returns (obs, privileged_obs)
LeggedRobot.check_termination combines termination contacts, the episode time-out and the roll and pitch cutoffs of 1.5 rad into one reset flag
X1DHStandCfg.env sets frame_stack=66, num_single_obs=47 and num_observations=3102
X1DHStandCfg.env sets c_frame_stack=3, single_num_privileged_obs=73 and num_privileged_obs=219
X1DHStandCfg.control sets action_scale=0.5 and decimation=10, and X1DHStandCfg.sim sets dt=0.001 s
X1DHStandCfg.init_state lists the 12 default joint angles in radians
X1DHStandCfgPPO sets the PPO training seed to 5
The environment imports isaacgym and torch
setup.py install_requires lists isaacgym, mujoco==2.3.6 and mujoco-python-viewer
The README says the repository is the reinforcement-learning training code for AgiBot X1, used with separate inference software for real-robot and simulated walking
The README documents MuJoCo sim2sim validation with scripts/sim2sim.py --task=x1_dh_stand
The environment is registered as x1_dh_stand through the in-tree task_registry, not gym.register

determinism.notes: the upstream resets and steps draw from torch's global RNG for domain randomization and command sampling; reset takes no seed and the environment exposes no get_state/set_state, so this package makes no replay claim

gaps: the fake backend is a pure-Python stand-in, not Isaac Gym: it models no rigid bodies, contacts, terrain, PD torques or MuJoCo model, and its joint, reward and termination values are placeholders

the real observation is a 3102-value history of 66 frames of 47 values and the privileged observation is 219 values; the fake returns arrays of those sizes but fills them from a 12-joint stand-in, so the layout and values are not the upstream observation

the fake does not model the upstream domain randomization, command resampling, push events, noise, reward terms or the contact/roll/pitch/time-out termination rules; it reports terminated only after its own placeholder episode length and truncation is always false
the action envelope is operator_required; site-limits.example.json supplies illustrative fake-scale bounds only, not a joint-angle or torque envelope; the fake does not model the PD controller
no integer RNG seed is exposed by the environment: reset takes no seed, the fake ignores seeds, and cap.world.seed.v1 is not bound
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
the upstream requires Isaac Gym, torch and a GPU (x1_dh_stand_env.py:35-40; setup.py:44-50), and neither the upstream simulator nor a real robot was run for this package
one environment is served; the shipped training config runs 4096 environments (x1_dh_stand_config.py:50), so vectorized training is not covered
only a fake backend exists: step passes Python lists, while LeggedRobot.step requires a torch.Tensor on the simulator device (legged_robot.py:115-118); a live factory must supply that adapter

live construction acquires Isaac Gym, changes process-wide torch JIT flags and creates the simulator and optional viewer (base_task.py:44-110); viewer close/QUIT calls sys.exit and render can block in fetch_results or sync_frame_time (base_task.py:155-177); no such live route is enabled

safe_state.description: the fake world has no autonomous simulation loop; the latch refuses new step and reset calls, and an in-flight step checks cancellation before each further tick; cached state stays readable
